name: Opendoor homepage: consumer landing page for its cash-offer home sale service
title: Opendoor homepage: consumer landing page for its cash-offer home sale service
answer: This is the consumer homepage of Opendoor, an iBuyer that buys homes directly. It is a marketing page rather than a technical or financial document. Its most useful statement for AI watchers is that Opendoor determines offers using real-time data, advanced pricing algorithms and on-the-ground expertise, analysing comparable sales, current market conditions and the home's features and condition, with an estimated cash offer in 24 hours and a final offer after an assessment. It names no model, no accuracy figure and no financial exposure.

sections.body: It is the public homepage of Opendoor, published by the company itself, with Opendoor Labs Inc. named in the accessibility statement at the foot of the page. It is a commercial landing page aimed at homeowners who want to sell, not a report, filing or technical document. Its scope is the offer process: how to request an offer, what the final offer includes, how pricing is described, how long each step takes, and how a seller can cancel. No publication or update date is stated. The text was harvested on 2026-09-27.
sections.heading: What this source is

sections.body: The page presents Opendoor as a way to sell a home without listing, showings or months of stress, closing on the seller's own timeline, with a free offer. It states that over 309,970 homeowners have been served by Opendoor, and carries three customer testimonials about speed, fairness and attention. It describes a Cash Now, More Later option that pairs a cash offer with the proceeds of a market transaction. The final offer is said to include the purchase price, a program fee for selling without staging or showings, a condition adjustment covering costs of preparing and reselling the home, title and escrow costs of 1 to 3 percent paid to third parties, and estimated net proceeds after all costs. On pricing, the page says Opendoor uses real-time data, advanced pricing algorithms and on-the-ground expertise, analysing comparable home sales, current market conditions and the home's specific features and condition, with a final offer issued after a home assessment. Sellers can cancel any time before closing without cost or penalty by contacting a Customer Experience Partner. An estimated cash offer arrives within 24 hours of entering an address and a few details, and a final offer within a few days of the assessment. The page closes with an accessibility statement and a support email address.
sections.heading: What it says

sections.body: The source states that over 309,970 homeowners have been served by Opendoor, without a date or definition for that figure. It states that title and escrow costs of 1 to 3 percent are paid to third parties. It states that an estimated cash offer comes within 24 hours of entering an address and a few details, and that a final offer follows within a few days of the home assessment. It states that a seller can cancel any time before closing without cost or penalty. It states that offers are determined using real-time data, advanced pricing algorithms and on-the-ground expertise. It gives no model names, no accuracy or error rates, and no financial figures beyond the fee percentages and the homeowner count.
sections.heading: Figures and claims worth noting

sections.body: This page is the consumer-facing entry point to the pricing process that the industry page treats as valuation AI with capital consequences. It is useful for seeing exactly what Opendoor tells sellers about how an offer is produced, which is a short statement about real-time data, advanced pricing algorithms and on-the-ground expertise, and for seeing the fee structure and timelines attached to that offer. It confirms that algorithms sit behind the price, and it shows the commercial framing around them. It does not carry the filings or documentation that would show the balance-sheet exposure, so it supports the existence of algorithmic pricing rather than any claim about its risk.
sections.heading: What it means for AI in Real Estate

sections.body: This is a commercial marketing page with no stated author, no date and no methodology. It gives no detail on the models, no training data, no accuracy or error rates, no discussion of pricing mistakes, and no financial statements or risk disclosures. The testimonials are selected customer quotes. The homeowner figure has no date or definition attached. Nothing here addresses regulation, valuation bias or balance-sheet exposure, so the filings and documentation referenced elsewhere are not contained in this source and cannot be assessed from it.
